title: How Did Hitler Get Power With Just 33%? 🗳️
description:
How did Hitler rise to power when he never won a majority in a free election? After his party slipped to 33% in November 1932, conservative insiders talked President Hindenburg into making him chancellor, and within eight weeks the Enabling Act let him rule without parliament.

Follow Zorbly for a new mystery every day.

pinned_comment: Who do you think really opened the door: the voters or the insiders?
topic: How did Hitler rise to power? (never won a majority; appointed by insiders, then the Reichstag Fire Decree and Enabling Act)
script:
Hitler never won a majority.
So how did he get handed Germany?
In 1929, the Great Depression hit.
By 1932, about six million Germans had no job.
Angry voters drifted to the extremes,
and his party peaked at 37 percent.
By November, it slipped to 33.
Then a few insiders made a deal.
They got President Hindenburg to name him chancellor,
sure they could control him.
One bragged he'd be squeezed into a corner within two months.
Four weeks later, the Reichstag burned.
A decree suspended basic rights.
In March, the Enabling Act let him make laws without parliament.
So who really opened the door?
key_facts: Nazi party won 37.3% (July 1932) and 33.1% (Nov 1932) in Reichstag elections; never a majority in a free election
About 6 million Germans registered unemployed in 1932

Hindenburg appointed Hitler chancellor on 30 January 1933 after a deal brokered by Franz von Papen and other conservatives, who believed they could control him; Papen is widely quoted as saying they would push Hitler into a corner within two months
Reichstag fire 27 February 1933; the next day's emergency decree suspended civil liberties incl. free press, free speech and assembly
Enabling Act passed 23 March 1933, 444 to 94, letting the cabinet make laws without parliament
